extracted.intended_audience: conference chairs, ethics chairs, ethics reviewers, authors, and general reviewers participating in ACL/ARR/ACL-affiliated conference peer review processes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizing, assigning, and writing ethics reviews for papers submitted to ACL/ARR and affiliated conferences, including what to flag, how to assess ethical concerns, and operational recommendations for chairs and committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess substantial ethical issues and potential for harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics reviews are meant to assess whether the submitted research exhibits any substantial ethical issues and could lead to harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics reviewing is critical to integrity and responsibility; reviewers should identify increased risk of harm outside current norms of NLP/CL research. This is the primary goal of ethics review — not a technical quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat ethics review as distinct from technical review
rubrics_metrics.description: An ethics review is not a scientific, nor a complete technical review. Your focus is only on the ethical issues and their presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not need to check equations, thoroughness of citations (except as they pertain to ethical issues), experimental design, or grammar/typos/writing style. Use the paper, supplement, and authors' checklist as inputs, but expect the paper to stand on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe issues in terms of the ACL code of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues, describe each in terms of the ACL code of ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot describe the issue in terms of the ACL code of ethics, consider whether it is a community-recognized issue. Refrain from relying on regional or national laws or practices since submissions may be from other countries; contact ACL ethics committee if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide actionable remediation suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ethical issue you identify, describe how you would suggest the authors address it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should not only flag problems but suggest concrete fixes (e.g., document permissions, remove PII, explain mitigations) so authors and chairs can act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological/approach ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify failures in the method or approach such as failure to consider or ameliorate negative impacts, biases, possible risks, and robustness/security concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not considering negative impacts on political/social/natural environment; failing to consider biases the approach may perpetuate; failing to consider robustness/security for systems close to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code, data, and people usage issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for failures related to use of code, data, or participation of people (e.g., missing informed consent, inadequate protection of personally identifiable information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also look for failures to respect intellectual property or data/code ownership, missing attribution/citation, violating licenses, and using artifacts inconsistent with their intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and model output harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the authors consider and attempt to ameliorate biases in data or biased code/model outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider downstream harms that biased outputs may cause and whether adequate mitigation or evaluation is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms from data/code/model release
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how datasets, code, or model outputs may cause harm when released or applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: releasing scraped private data without removing PII, enabling abusive applications, or disseminating models that facilitate harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker/annotator welfare and remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether participation of people (e.g., annotators, microworkers) in the research may cause benefits or harms, and whether compensation is fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For microworking crowdsourcing, the paper should state how a fair rate of pay was determined and how researchers ensured fair compensation; reviewers may ask whether payment was adequate and appropriate to local contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and privacy protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for proper informed consent and adequate protection of personally identifiable information as required by relevant ethics norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should document consent procedures, anonymization/de-identification steps, and policies for handling sensitive or identifying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property, attribution, and license compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that authors respect IP and data/code ownership, properly cite creators of artifacts, and use artifacts under permissible licenses and terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If artifacts are redistributed, check license compatibility and whether use was consistent with creators' intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual use and intended/potential applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess risks related to intended or potential applications (dual use) and whether the paper discusses mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for discussion of how applications could harm individuals, groups, or society and whether authors propose mitigations or restrictions (e.g., not releasing models/data) where risks are unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic dishonesty and integrity violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify instances of dishonesty in execution or presentation: plagiarism, deliberate violation of anonymity/citation/review, duplicate submission, falsifying results, or misrepresentation of authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to code of ethics provisions (e.g., strive for high quality in processes and products), request correction, attribution, or other remedies as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid basing ethics judgements on regional laws alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from relying on regional or national laws or practices in ethics reviews since submissions may come from other jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What governs acceptable practice in ACL venues is the ACL code of ethics; where relevant, reviewers may refer to broader human rights documents (e.g., Universal Declaration of Human Rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of ethics chairs' purview
rubrics_metrics.description: The purview of Ethics Chairs should be limited to reviewing the ethical issues in the execution of the research presented in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics chairs should not overreach into general technical assessment; however, they may expect authors to state legal access to data in ethics sections or submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial assessment and triage of flagged papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a quick check to decide which flagged papers really need a full ethics review; consult justifications and optionally read abstract or paper if in doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an 'Instructions' sheet of common false flags/patterns; false flags (e.g., justification 'None') generally do not require full review. Consider whether flagger/authors benefit from a brief note if no full review is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require clear justification when flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers/AE's should provide a clear and succinct justification when flagging a paper for full ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many flagged papers lack justifications ('N/A', 'None'), which burdens ethics chairs; clear justifications help assign appropriate reviewers and reduce false positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not flag solely for missing sections or checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing ethical considerations/limitations sections or incompletely filled checklists do not by themselves justify a full ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These issues can be flagged to AEs/reviewers via the reviewer checklist or called out in the review/meta-review; only flag for full ethics review when substantive ethical concerns are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not automatically flag for copyright/consent/transparency issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright, consent, or transparency concerns alone do not always warrant a full ethics review; these can often be addressed in the reviewer or meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these issues require deeper investigation, provide specific reasons in the justification when flagging for a full ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid blanket assumptions when flagging (common misconceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid assuming that certain classes of papers automatically require full ethics review (e.g., all data-centric papers, any use of human annotators, papers on sensitive topics, high-stakes domain papers, or papers on NLP ethics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess context, safeguards reported, and whether specific concerns (e.g., engaging marginalized communities, traumatizing annotations, regulatory non-compliance) justify a deeper ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for Responsible NLP Research — limitations and risks reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should describe limitations and potential risks of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps pre-empt reviewer questions and serves as a FAQ; reviewers use the checklist information as one factor in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — artifact citation, license, and intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should cite creators of scientific artifacts, discuss licenses or terms for use/distribution, and indicate whether their use is consistent with intended use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that redistribution is permitted and that use adheres to creators' restrictions; require documentation where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — PII, offensive content checks and anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should describe steps taken to check whether data contains PII or offensive content and describe steps to protect or anonymize it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check for documentation and evidence of adequate anonymization/PII protection before data/model release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — documentation and descriptive statistics of artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide documentation and descriptive statistics of datasets and artifacts used in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes provenance, collection protocol, demographics, and other metadata that contextualizes potential biases and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — compute and experimental reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For computational experiments, authors should report number of parameters, total computational budget (e.g., GPU hours), computing infrastructure, and experimental setup (including hyperparameter search and best-found values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should report descriptive statistics about results and whether they used existing packages; these details support reproducibility and assessment of environmental/resource impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — human participants reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For work involving human participants, report full text of instructions given, recruitment source (platform, students), payment details, consent procedures, IRB approval/exemption status, and basic demographic/geographic characteristics of annotator population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information allows assessment of participant welfare, consent adequacy, and representativeness; discuss whether payments were adequate to local contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist — use of AI assistants disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should disclose use of AI assistants in producing the work submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider whether use of AI assistants affects authorship, accountability, or reproducibility and whether disclosure aligns with venue policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational: recruit ethics chairs early and allocate time
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics chairs should be recruited early in planning with sufficient time to participate in setting review schedule to ensure time for ethics review and clarity about referral and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate at least 2–3 weeks in the review timeline for ethics review, and set a strict cut-off for when ACs/SACs may flag papers for ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational: ensure adequate ethics reviewer pool and assignment loads
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure an adequately sized ethics reviewer pool proportional to submission volume; historically ~4% of submissions get full ethics review; recommend ~5% planning rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each paper needs one ethics review. Assuming ~2.5 papers/reviewer, plan reviewer count accordingly, monitor trends, and add reviewers if expertise gaps arise. Respect reviewer-claimed reduced loads and avoid overassigning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational: use master tracking and consoles
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarize with OpenReview consoles and maintain a master tracking sheet (timeline, instructions, reviewers, chairs coordination, papers tracking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Ethics Chairs console and Ethics Reviewer console; keep records of availability, assignments, and Paper Status. Add new reviewers to tracking sheet and use provided recruitment templates/forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational: owner assignment and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign an owner ethics chair for each flagged paper who coordinates the initial assessment, reviewer assignment, and follow-up to ensure reviews are submitted by deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner should follow up with reviewers nearer the deadline (direct email often more effective than platform reminders). Update Papers Tracking sheet continuously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational: limit per-reviewer load
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid assigning more than 2–4 ethics papers per reviewer (depending on cycle) and respect any reduced loads requested by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track assigned loads in the Reviewers sheet and consult availability before assigning; update system assignments in OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational: handle inflow, duplicates, and removals
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor daily inflow of flagged papers, detect duplicates, and track removals when flags are retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spreadsheet formulas or scripts to batch-transfer flagged papers; maintain active/inactive status column; be aware of influxes aligned with technical review deadlines and plan workflow accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and transparency of process
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the ethics review process (publicize recommendations in advance) and collect metrics: number of flagged papers, reviewed for ethics, accepted conditionally, rejected on ethical grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicize process at least one month in advance; maintain documentation to help future chairs estimate workload and to increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a large and diverse ethics committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a large and diverse committee including participants from different countries/continents and varied gender representation; consider term limits and pairing less experienced with experienced reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To mitigate institutional/government pressure, consider assigning papers to reviewers from other countries; rotating membership and term limits encourage diversity of perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include ethics guidance in Calls for Papers and across tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPs should incorporate ethics guidelines and make clear that submissions may be rejected due to ethical concerns; apply guidelines uniformly across all conference tracks (main, student, industrial, workshops, tutorials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit ethics requirements can deter straightforward ethical issues (e.g., unpaid annotations) and ensure consistent expectations for all submissions including workshops archived in the Anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data scraping and redistribution considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between reusing existing scraped datasets (without redistributing) and scraping new ones intended for distribution; authors should document permissions and intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For newly scraped datasets intended for distribution, require documentation of permission and careful PII removal before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ascribing identity characteristics without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid treating identity characteristics as reliably ascribable (e.g., inferring from names) or as fixed categorical properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about labeling or inferring identity; consider the ethical implications and uncertainty in such annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to calculate and publish how much energy experiments or methodologies require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emerging best practices include reporting energy consumption or compute budgets to make environmental impacts visible and comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational platform and workflow improvements suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure conference platforms (SoftConf/OpenReview) are configured/tested for ethics workflows: easy sharing of flagged submissions, ability to notify when ethics reviews are submitted, and separation of ethics vs technical track assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend platform features: explicit ethics review track, notifications for ethics review submissions, ability to communicate with ethics reviewers, and functionality to manage ethics workflow without external spreadsheets.
